transcript.text: The sides of our new fridge freezer get really warm, almost hot, especially near the front edge. Is that a fire risk? It's in an alcove between two units.

Warm or even quite hot sides—especially near the front edges—are often normal on modern fridge freezers. Many models put the condenser pipes in the side walls, and the heat helps prevent condensation around the doors. A new appliance may also run warmer for the first 24–48 hours while it reaches temperature.

It should not normally be a fire risk if it is installed with the manufacturer’s required ventilation gaps. An alcove can be a problem if the sides, rear or top are too close to surrounding units, because the heat cannot escape and the compressor has to work harder.

What to do:

• Check the installation instructions for your exact model and follow its stated clearance around the sides, back and top. Do not assume it can be fitted tightly between units just because it physically fits.
• Make sure any vents at the back, base or top are not blocked, and do not pack items on top or around it.
• Ensure the plug and socket are cool, secure and undamaged; avoid extension leads or overloaded adaptors.
• Leave enough room to open the doors fully and avoid the cabinet sides constantly touching adjacent furniture.

“Hot but you can keep your hand there briefly” can be normal. Switch it off and seek advice from the retailer/manufacturer or an appliance engineer if it is too hot to touch, the surrounding units are becoming unusually hot or discoloured, there is a burning smell, buzzing/crackling, smoke, a hot plug/socket, or it trips the electrics. If there is smoke or a burning smell, unplug it if safe to do so and contact emergency services if there is any sign of fire.

If you provide the make/model and the gaps around the appliance, I can help interpret the installation requirements.

It's a Hotpoint H7X 93T SK, about 2 months old. The gaps are only about 1cm each side, and the cupboard above has a few cm gap. I can keep my hand on the sides, it's warm like a radiator on low, and there's no burning smell. Is that gap enough?

The warmth you describe sounds normal for this type of fridge freezer: the H7X range uses the cabinet sides to shed heat, so they can feel like a low radiator, particularly around the front/door-edge area. With no burning smell, electrical symptoms, or surfaces becoming too hot to touch, it does not sound like an immediate fire risk.

However, 1 cm at each side is unlikely to be adequate unless Hotpoint’s installation instructions for that exact model explicitly permit it. This is a freestanding appliance, not an integrated one designed to be tightly enclosed. Restricted airflow can make it run hotter and longer, increase energy use and noise, and shorten compressor life.

For the H7X 93T SK, check the installation section of the supplied/manual documentation for the specified clearances. As a practical rule, it should have:

• clear air space at the sides and above — commonly several centimetres rather than 1 cm;
• the required gap behind it, often around 5 cm for freestanding fridge freezers;
• no blocked ventilation route at the top/rear of the alcove.

A cupboard only a few centimetres above may also be marginal, especially if the alcove is otherwise enclosed. There needs to be a way for warm air to rise and escape rather than collect above and behind the appliance.

So: warm sides are expected; the tight alcove fit is the part worth addressing. Pull it forward enough to meet the manual’s rear clearance, confirm the side/top requirements, and ideally increase the side gaps if possible. If you cannot meet the stated clearances, ask Hotpoint support or the installer whether that alcove installation is approved for the model—don’t rely on it merely fitting physically.

I'd rather not pull it out, as the floor is brand new and I'm worried about scratching it. The manual does say to leave space, but I haven't checked exactly how much. Is there anything I can do without moving it?

Yes—there are a few sensible checks you can do without pulling it out, but none truly replaces the clearance Hotpoint specifies.

1. Measure the gaps accurately
   Use a ruler or tape measure at several points, especially near the back where the appliance may sit closer to the units. Measure the space:
• each side;
• above the fridge;
• behind it, if you can see or reach enough to estimate;
• around any grille/vent at the base or rear.

2. Check that no ventilation openings are obstructed
   Make sure nothing is wedged beside, behind, on top of, or under the fridge freezer—packaging, bags, stored items, skirting/trim, or a plinth can interfere with airflow.

3. Keep the cupboard above clear
   Don’t fill the small space above the appliance with items, cloths, boxes, etc. If the cupboard/alcove has a rear panel and traps hot air, that is more significant than the warmth of the sides themselves.

4. Keep it clean around the base
   Dust build-up around lower vents can reduce airflow. With the appliance unplugged, you may be able to vacuum carefully around the accessible base/side areas without moving it. Don’t poke tools into vents or disturb wiring.

5. Monitor for warning signs
   Your current description���warm, hand can remain on it, no smell—is reassuring. Act promptly if the casing becomes painful to touch, the nearby cabinet starts getting very hot/discoloured, it runs almost continuously, cooling performance worsens, or the plug/socket becomes warm.

That said, if the manual calls for more than 1 cm at the sides or more space above/behind, the long-term answer is to reposition it or alter the alcove/ventilation. A fan, leaving doors open, or turning the thermostat colder will not solve inadequate condenser airflow and may make matters worse.

If moving it becomes necessary, protect the new floor rather than dragging it: empty it first, use purpose-made appliance/furniture sliders or a thin hardboard sheet, and have a second person help. Many retailers/installation services can also reposition it safely. Avoid tipping it significantly; if it has to be laid on its side, follow Hotpoint’s guidance and allow it to stand upright for several hours before switching it back on.
